To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully synthesized two novel fluorinated copolypers by grafting ω -hydroxyl pyrazole (trip) and triazole (trit) tripods on poly(CTFE - alt -IEVE), which have good thermal properties and high proton conductivities.

we have successfully synthesized two new proton exchange membranes based on azole heterocycles and poly(chlorotrifiuoroethylene-alt-2-iodo-ethyl vinyl ether) by a two-step process, and the membranes showed good thermal stability, good proton conductivity and high electrochemical stability.
new fluorinated copolymer containing azole groups was synthesized and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new family of proton conducting membranes for fuel cells based on poly(CTFE) copolymers grafted with azole tripods.
the design of new proton-conducting materials based on the grafting of pyrazole and trizole groups onto a fluorinated polymer.
the development of new copolymers containing nitrogen heterocycles for proton conducting membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these new copolymers have a high degree of grafting and are thermally and electrochemically stable.
the pyrazole-based copolymer is a promising candidate for fuel cell application.
the pyrazole-based membrane is more stable than the triazole-based membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
poly(CTFE-alt-IEVE)-dep-Trip 80% copolymer is a promising material to be used in polymer electrolyte fuel cell membranes.
the proton conductivity of the new copolymers is not as good as that of the Nafion membrane, but they are stable in a wide range of temperature and humidity.
the proton conductivity of poly(CTF-IEVE)- dep- Triazol- 28% copolymer is higher than poly(CTFE) and poly(CTE) membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of pyrazolic groups in the copolymer structure is an interesting strategy for improving proton conductivity.
the pyrazole group is a better proton conductor than the triazole group.
these new copolymers are promising materials for fuel cell membranes and could be used as an additive in Nafion® membranes to improve the performance of the membrane.
